findings.description: The exact Quote Date formula and its numeric encoding are pure code-side surplus invisible in SHEET-MARK-004's text. The spec says only 'stamp each cached mark with GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date, not the wall-clock read time' — it says nothing about needing a distinct companion formula/column, nor about HOW the date is encoded. The real code (lib.rs:259-274, `quote_date_formula`) pins an exact string: `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — truncate `tradetime` via `INT`, re-base to days-since-1970-01-01 (matching the kernel's own `Date` epoch) by subtracting `DATE(1970,1,1)`, render via `TEXT(...,"0")` as a digits-only locale-invariant string, and degrade to `""` via `IFERROR` while loading/errored. All three B-runs reproduce this formula verbatim (B1 #3-4, B2 #2-4, B3 #2-3) — strong, independently-converged evidence this is real, load-bearing behavior the one-line EARS text never states.

The state machine governing WHEN a quote_date is set, preserved, or withheld is entirely unstated by the spec, which only describes the single 'settled numeric read' case. The real code (`read_marks`, lib.rs:817-887) pins: while Transient/absent within `SettleConfig.max_polls` (default 8), keep polling without touching any mark; once the window elapses with a PRIOR mark, carry the ENTIRE prior `Mark` forward unchanged (price_cents AND quote_date together, not just the date) and do NOT record it degraded; with no prior mark, degrade `TimedOut` (no mark, no quote_date); a `Permanent` reading degrades immediately regardless of any prior mark (terminal errors never carry forward — only transients do). Verified against tests `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window`, `no_prior_mark_stays_transient_degrades_after_window`, and `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry` (marks.rs:161-241). All three B-runs converge on this taxonomy (B1 #5-8, B2 #6-8, B3 #5-7).

`MarksProduced::to_ledger_marks()` (lib.rs:337-346) drops degraded symbols entirely — no synthetic quote_date-less placeholder is projected into the ledger `Marks` map, confirmed by `degraded_symbol_absent_from_ledger_marks_for_per_symbol_degradation` (marks.rs:266-313), which also asserts the downstream ledger-core replay treats the omitted symbol as per-symbol-degraded (`unrealized_cents.is_none()`). SHEET-MARK-004 says nothing about this projection boundary; captured explicitly in B1 #9 and implicitly folded into B2/B3's degrade-handling items.

Weaker/less-unanimous: the settle pass propagates a transport-level `Err` from `read_price_pass` rather than emitting an empty marks set or itself carrying `prior` forward (lib.rs:806-816; test `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks`, marks.rs:131-159). Only B3 states this as its own numbered item (#8); B1 and B2 don't surface it as a distinct requirement, so it's real and verified but less stable across the three B-runs than findings 1-3.

notes: Direction A produced no genuine findings. All three A-runs invent the same basic architecture — a fallible `stamp_mark`/`settle_mark` function that parses a raw sheet-cell string into a calendar `NaiveDate`, erroring (never defaulting to `Utc::now()`) on missing/unparseable input — but this entire apparatus has no basis in the one-line EARS text, which never mentions a companion cell, a parse step, or error semantics for a missing date. Per the classification rule, unanimous A-side invention with no textual basis is an assumption artifact, not a finding. Notably the three A-runs are NOT fully convergent even on their own invented details: A1 assumes ISO `%Y-%m-%d`, A2 assumes US-locale `%m/%d/%Y`, and A3 sidesteps parsing altogether by taking a pre-parsed `Option<NaiveDate>` — a real (if narrow) three-way disagreement on the date-string format, which is why aAgreement is rated medium rather than high. None of the three anticipated the real code's actual representation: `pt_core::Date`, an integer day-count matching the 1970-01-01 epoch baked directly into the `GOOGLEFINANCE` formula's own `INT(...)-DATE(1970,1,1)` arithmetic, with no calendar-string parsing at this layer at all (the `sheets-view` crate never parses a date string — `PriceReading::Numeric` already carries a resolved `Date`). Checked every concrete B-side claim (the formula text, the carry-forward/degrade taxonomy, the ledger-projection exclusion, the transport-failure propagation) against `lib.rs` and `tests/marks.rs` directly; all verified verbatim, no B-side fabrication found. B2's item #10 (SubCent/Permanent price-conversion degrade) and B3's item #9 (settle-pass-strictly-after-write ordering) are accurate to the code but tangential to SHEET-MARK-004 specifically (they're about price conversion and write/read sequencing, not date-stamping), so I did not count them as core drift findings for this requirement.
